input: Given question: Smith is an external auditor and his total meal entertainment expenditure in an FBT year is $ 90,000. The firm does not maintain a 12-week register and the firm estimates 30% of the meal entertainment expenditure was provided to Smith as a fringe benefit. What should be the taxable value of meal entertainment fringe benefit in this scenario? Option A: $ 30,000 Option B: $ 27,000 Option C: $ 45,000 Option D: None of the above The correct answer is Option C.
reference: If Div 9A is chosen by the employer to compute the taxable value of meal entertainment fringe benefit for the year of tax then it can follow either: 1. The 50/50 split method (s 37BA) - under this method, the taxable value of the meal entertainment fringe benefit is 50% of the expenses incurred by the employer in providing meal entertainment benefits to all persons.  2. The 12-week register method (s 37B) - under this method, the taxable value of the meal entertainment fringe benefit is determined b reference to a 12-week register kept by the employer to determine the employer's percentage of meal entertainment fringe benefits. In the above question as there is no register being maintained by the firm, therefore, the taxable value of the meal entertainment fringe benefit provided is $90,000 x 50% = $ 45,000.

reference: No GST charged on the value in respect of GST free supplies. GST free supplies. Note: GST -free suppliers are excluded from the definition of taxable supplies. The key point is the primary function of the nursery is to provide child-minding services rather than providing an education. Reference: Case of Dixon v FC of T 97 ATC 4762. The Commissioner contended that the primary function of the nursery school was to provide child-minding services rather than providing an education. The taxpayer's argument that the children were receiving education was not accepted by the court. The court found that the child-minding was the main function of the nursery school and the education provided was merely incidental. Reference: Barkoczy, S. (2017). input: Given question: Mr. Chugh is from India and now is an Australian resident for tax purposes. In 2017, he signed an agreement in Rome with a company to render services in France and goes to France to render those services to Australia for 6 months. His source of income would be? Option A: Australia Option B: India Option C: Rome Option D: France Option E: None of the above The correct answer is Option D.
reference: The Answer is France, based on FCT v French (1957); FCT v Efstathakis (1979), the source of income would be recognised as the place where the performance of services occurs Info - If an taxpayer is a foreign resident, the taxpayer is taxed only taxed on ordinary and statutory income sourced in Australia, unless deemed assessable income on some other basis.Source rules based on a combination of common law principles and statutory provisions.Practically, it requires classification of income into different classes to determine source. Categories of Income1. Sale of goods (trading stock):         - Generally, the place where the trading activities take place.2. Sale of property other than trading stock:         - For real property, the place where the property is located.3. Services:         - Generally, the place where the performance of services occurs: FCT v French (1957); FCT v Efstathakis (1979).4. Interest:         - Emphasis on the place where the contract for the loan was made and where the money was advanced: Spotless Services v FCT (1993).5. Dividends:         - The place where the company derived its profits: Esquire Nominees Ltd v FCT (1973).6. Royalties:         - The place where the location of the industrial or intellectual property from which the royalty flows.
best_explanation: source of income is France because he is working there for 6 months. even though he is an Indian resident, his income will be taxable in France because he is working there. in this way, he will be paying taxes to France and will be getting benefit from there as well. this is how it works when it comes to source of income. a person is supposed to pay taxes to the country where he is working.
